about: What scripts/prepare-assets.mjs copies out of the original game's extraction into public/assets (gitignored). Paths in src are relative to the extraction. sounds -> sounds/<id>.wav (eager: in lib/audioCatalog.ts SOUNDS, preloaded; on-demand: fetched when first played). voices -> sounds/voice/<id>.wav, always on demand, with the transcript as the original pak has it (Windows-1252, verbatim; null where it has none) and the FEATURE_PLAN.md item that wires the line (use: bark or campaign). lore -> sounds/lore/<id>.wav, a copy of the voice line it names. anims -> anims/<id>.json from animations/. objrig -> props/objrig/<id>.obj and .mtl from models/.

voices.text: Greetings! I am Richard the Strong, and I welcome you to LEGO Creator Knights' Kingdom.
To unlock the power of the Kingdom and become a soldier in Leo's court, you must complete the first four challenges.
Don’t worry. I’ll be here to help you throughout.
I'll use this challenge arrow to show you which buttons to press.
I’ll introduce you to some friends and foes along the way!

Right then! Are you ready for action? 
To move forward in the LEGO world, move the mouse pointer to anywhere along the top edge of your screen and hold it there. 
Go on, you do it! Follow me now!
Did you keep up alright? Good! Right! I want to introduce you to the evil Cedric the Bull.
He's right at the end of this line.
To move right, move the mouse pointer to the right edge of your screen and hold it there. Are you ready to meet him? Do it now!
That’s it. I see you are getting the hang of things!
My name is Cedric the Bull!
Don't listen to what they say. I should be ruling the Knights' Kingdom!
I’ll let you in on a secret but I don’t want Leo to hear.

Do what I tell you. 
Click and hold the zoom button down until you are really, really close. It’s the button with the plus sign on it.
That's better! The truth is, unless they find a good castle builder soon, I'll be King myself tomorrow!
Ignore Cedric!  Let me see Richard's new recruit!
Listen to me now! Move the mouse pointer to the left edge of your screen to move left. Do that now.
I am King Leo. Do do you like my castle? Richard tells me you want to become a knight.
My land is a wonderful place, but for Cedric and his gang. He’s always trying to get his hands on my Kingdom... and his bottom on my throne!
For now though, Cedric still lives in the woods!
Hello we've not seen you before!  Come and meet me.
Move the mouse cursor to the left of the screen, as you've done before.
You've met my husband. He can be a bit pompous you know! A fine king though!
I am Queen Leonora and I advise Leo on tactics.
Have you met my daughter Princess Storm? Maybe later. Few can match her skills with a sword.
OK Back to me again now! Let me introduce you to John of Mayne.
Move the mouse pointer to the left edge of your screen again.

John is my right hand man, a bit shy but a fine and gallant knight!
Right then, that’s the introductions done!

Did you know some people and vehicles can move about in the LEGO world? 
This will happen whenever the Play button is on.
Click on the Play button now.
Well done! Notice the green light on the play button when it's on. King Leo's off to run the Kingdom, and Cedric, well it’s anybody’s guess what he’s gone off to do.
Let’s go and see what’s happening at the castle!
Move the mouse pointer to the top of the screen and move forward to the drawbridge.
Now we need to open the drawbridge to get into the castle.
To be able to open and close things you have to click on the Action button above. Click it now.
Good! Now we are able to open the drawbridge! Ready for some action?
Click the drawbridge to open it.
Ah, there you are! How did I get in?
Erm, I used the back door! You’ll need to use this the big gate, we call it a Portcullis!
Click on the portcullis to open it!
Well done! At this rate you’ll soon be a Knight of the realm!

Congratulations on finishing the first challenge. 

Here you learnt how to move about the LEGO world by moving the mouse to the edges of the screen. 

You learnt how to zoom, and now you know how to click the Action button to make models do things! 

Remember we also found how turning on the play button allows models to start moving of their own accord.
Welcome back!
King Leo has asked me to build extra defenses. I don't believe Cedric will be brave enough to show up again, but you are just in time to help.
Haha!  Nobody can defy Cedric the Bull. Your defences are useless!
Ow! Let's shut Cedric up! See the play button is on? Click that off right now!
Stop the play button! He's giving me a headache!
Phew! Thank goodness for that!
With the play button stopped only the helper can move, and that's me!
Right. We need to build a wall. We get our models from the Model Bucket above.
Click on the Model Bucket to open it.
Great! There’s just the one wall for now but it will be full of things after we finish the challenges.
Build all you want to! Nothing will stop me!

I'm going to tell you how to bring in the wall. You do it as I explain. To bring the wall into the LEGO world, click it and keep the mouse button down as you move the pointer back over the world. An outline will appear on the pointer to help you place the wall.
Just let go when the wall is near me. We call this mouse action ‘click and drag’.
That’s the way! Now try to drag it onto the flashing target.
Click on the model and drag it towards the flashing target.
Try to get the wall right on the target.
Right! now we need to turn that wall the right way round! I'll just do a quick magic trick to show what I mean!
Just something a wizard once taught me!
Click on the Turn Model button the challenge arrow is pointing at, then click on the wall.  Each time you click the wall,it turns another step.
The panel with the turn-model button in is called the ‘Toolbar’.
Only one of the toolbar buttons can be on at any one time. Clicking on one turns the others off. With me so far? Good! Let’s move the wall forward a bit.
Try to move the wall onto the new target.
Whoops! That was my fault! I forgot to remind you that you need to press the Move button first! I'll turn the wall back again so we can start that bit again.
Click on the Move button and then try to move the brick on top of the mark.

Wonderful! Well done! You’ve finished the second challenge. You’re flying through these! 
You’ve now learned more about the Play button, how to get models in from the Model Bucket and move and turn them in the world.
From the noise of sawing in the forest, I think Cedric is up to something!
Hmm! Maybe we'll need more than just walls to protect the castle!
Can you find a cannon for me?
Click the Model Bucket above.
Excellent! Well remembered!
The bucket has six sections. Weapons that don't move (like the cannon we are looking for) will be in the section shown by the big bomb!
Click on the big bomb now!
There’s just the one cannon for now. It will be full of stuff later! Now we need to bring the cannon in.
Remember, when you click and drag a model in, hold your left mouse button down and let go when the outline is where you want the model to be.
Click and drag the cannon to where the target's flashing.
Hmm! We've put it a bit far away there.
Try to move it onto the target.
There, that should keep Cedric and his gang away! Excellent!
Right! Now, the higher a cannon is, the further it can fire.
So let's put it on the raised platform. I'll show you how first!
By keeping a finger on the Control key on your keyboard while moving models, they'll move up and down in the LEGO world. Your Control key probably has the letters 'Ctrl' on it.
Look at the keyboard picture to see which key to press.
Now for your turn! Drag the cannon up higher. Remember to use the keyboard Control key with the left mouse button pressed down.
Good! Can you see the shadow? You can use the shadow to see exactly what is below the cannon.
If I move the cannon over the platform, can you see how the shadow tells me when the platform is exactly below?
Now you need to put the cannon down on top of the platform. Ready? Go!
Just press and hold the Control key while holding the left mouse button down as we did before, and drag the cannon down onto the platform.
Oops! Remember the Control key for moving models up and down.
Let’s try again!
Haha, that'll keep Cedric at bay! Super work! You’ve finished the third challenge!
Now you can move models anywhere in the world, sideways, forwards and back, and up and down, and you can find different types of models in the model bucket.
To make some models easier to place on each other, they actually snap together when they get close!
The castle and tower are like that, and that helps you build quickly when you're in a hurry! Talking of which, I can’t hear any sawing in the forest anymore. I wonder what Cedric was doing?
Goodness me! So that was what Cedric was up to, he’s built an attack tower. He still thinks he can take the castle!
Hey! I think a well aimed cannon shot should send him running.
Do you remember the Action Button made the drawbridge work? Well how about the cannon!
Click on the Action button now.
Super! Now our cannon can be fired!
Click on the cannon to fire at the attack tower!

Haha! Congratulations, a first class shot! 
That’ll put an end to Cedric’s latest plans!
Now here’s a new way to explore the LEGO World.
The ball with four green arrows on it lets you move around in a big circle, and look down on the LEGO world from above.
Click on the ball's centre and drag it in different directions - you'll soon get the hang of it!
The further you turn the ball the faster you move.
When you want to look at a different model click the Target button and then that model. Try that now...
Good!
Now when you use the view ball in the middle, it's centred on the object you've just clicked.
Try experimenting for a short while.
To zoom the view, use the Plus and Minus keys (like we used to look at Cedric in the very first challenge).

Can you see the giant catapult. This is called a ‘mobile trebuchet’, but that’s so difficult to say that I’ll just call it a catapult! 

Use what we've learned in all the challenges so far to move to the catapult.
Can you fire it?
Move to the catapult and click on it to fire! Remember the Action button.
Let’s see what happens if we click on the Play button. Try that now!
Wow! How about that! All the soldiers are marching together! That’s fantastic!
Lets keep this game to play another day! Follow my steps to save the game. First let's stop the world moving.
Click the Play button to switch it off.
When we save the world by clicking the Floppy Disk button, it shows all our other saved worlds. In this challenge there'll only be this one, so simply click the Tick button to return.
Click the Floppy Disk button now, and then the Tick button.

Well done!
You’ve completed the first four challenges and are now a fully-fledged soldier in King Leo’s court! 
Now you know how to fire weapons and move about throughout the Knights' Kingdom using all the advanced controls, and save your world to use again later!
Now you can build a world and get it when you want to play with it again.
Of course there’s lots more to explore. If you want to know what a button does you can simply click on the picture of me in the bottom right corner, and I'll tell you how it works.

All of the kingdom is now open to you! When you feel ready and if you want to try making your own models click the hammer to enter the workshop. There are two more challenges there and mastery will bring you a Knighthood.

Farewell now. 
Enjoy the kingdom!
Hello again!
You know. I've been thinking. It’s no good catching Cedric if we've got nowhere to lock him up! Time to build a jail, and here's a good spot!
I've a good idea of what we need. Let’s go into the Workshop and I'll show you.
To go into the Workshop, click on the hammer button now.
Excellent! I'm quite proud of my idea. Here’s what it’s going to look like when we’ve finished it. Not bad eh!
So let’s get started. We need to build the wall up at the back before we put the window with bars in.
I've put a brick in the Brick Bucket that’s just the right size. You are going to get it for me and place it in front of the doorway.
I'm going to help you by flashing a red brick in the place where we'd like it to go.

Click and Drag the brick onto the baseplate now. 
Remember, only let go of the mouse button when you want to drop the brick and when you see the white outline.
Now you want to connect our brick to the back wall (where I'm flashing the help brick).
When you want to move the brick up or down, remember to use the Control key on your keyboard, at the same time as clicking with the mouse.
Ready? Try to place the brick in position now.
Well done!
We need two more of those on top of it, where I'm flashing the help brick!
This is easy because it's just a quick copy of our first brick!
Click on the Copy Brick button above.
That’s it!
Click our brick to Copy it.
Well done!
Click on our brick to Copy it a second time!
Notice that a copied brick floats just above the bricks below.
Drag both the bricks downward to join them. Remember to use the Control key!
Well done!
A good jail needs windows and doors with strong bars in them!
Can you tell which button in the Brick Bucket to click on to see windows and doors?
Click on the Windows and Doors button now.
Good! As you can see in the Brick Bucket there's a window and a door.
Put the window with the bars in it on top of our last brick.
Hah! That’s not a jail - it's got no door!
Good Point! Just add the door now, as Cedric reminded us! I'll flash the help brick in the right place.
Why? Why? Why did I open my big mouth!
Okay! Click on the Basic brick button in the Brick Bucket.
You'll see I've put the things we need for the flat roof here.
We'll drag the bricks in just as we did before, but I'll show you first.
I'll move the roof plates into position, but instead of the Control Key, I'll hold the Shift Key down as I move the brick.
See! The brick magically climbed over the bricks below it!... Your turn!
Try and put both roof pieces in position now.
Well done! I'll add a few battlements. Just to finish it off!
Oh No!
You did very well.
One thing that I’ve been doing to help you so far is making sure that you don't accidentally move or turn bricks that you’ve already put in place.
Normally when you move your mouse pointer over a brick it will choose that brick and all the bricks that sit on top of it. This is really useful when you build difficult models.
Well, you're only one challenge away from being a Knight of the Kingdom! In this challenge you learnt how to construct your own models and use the bricks in the Brick bucket.
When you’ve finished, click on the button with a picture of a broom on it. This will sweep away your model.
In the final challenge we shall learn how to paint and save models and use them in our LEGO world. We'll soon have Cedric safely behind bars!
Right, nearly finished! This is the last challenge. Let's paint the jail before we place it in the LEGO world.
We'll paint the door, window and the battlements (the fiddly bits on the roof).
Click on the paint button above.
Just click on a colour on this paint palette and then on the brick you want to paint. It's as simple as that!
Paint the door, the window and the battlements now.

Super! Now let's save the jail so we can use it in the Kingdom. 

We'll do this by clicking the Floppy Disk button. This shows all our other saved models. 

In this challenge there'll only be this one so simply click the Tick Button to return.
Click the Floppy Disk button now and then the Tick button!
Good!
Well done! Now we have a model jail to use whenever we want it!
Let's put the jail in the LEGO world!
Click on the Door button to leave the Workshop.
To find our jail, open the Model Bucket and click on the hand holding a brick.
Great! This section is where all our workshop models are kept.
Click and drag the jail into the world and place it on the flashing target!

Well done!
You have competed all the challenges and truly shown yourself worthy to be a Knight in our realm! 

There's lots, lots more to do and discover and many things you will need to study the instruction manual to discover, things like driving a vehicle or flying a dragon!
If you ever need to know more about a button just click on the picture of me in the bottom corner and then the button. I’ll do everything I can to help you.
Farewell, my good Knight!
